body.statement: Fix \(N\), \(K\), and \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\), and restrict the input to a rational tensor \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), supplied either with its exact entries or by a rational law \(p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\) inducing those entries. Characterize the cone \(\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\) on this feasible domain and hence the label-free set \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\): equivalently, decide whether some common unit relabelling \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) makes \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\mathrm{id})\geq\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\sigma)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal M_N^K\) and every \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\). Derive a recognition algorithm polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and the rational input bit length that returns such a relabelling and a finite cut certificate on yes instances, and returns arm-specific binary ordered columns together with \(\sigma\) giving a strict exact loss improvement on no instances; if binary separation is not complete, characterize the minimal finite alphabet required for a complete separating certificate.
body.justification: The residual question isolates computational structure after the feasible-domain mathematics has been characterized exactly.
body.gap: Polynomial-time recognition or a faithful hardness result, together with binary completeness or a minimal-alphabet characterization, remains open.
body.consumer: A solution would turn the current exact but exhaustive audit into a scalable design certificate with standardized failure witnesses.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct an algorithm polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and rational input bit length for orbit membership in \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\), with the requested relabelling and finite yes certificate and a binary no witness; alternatively prove a faithful complexity obstruction on the admissible balanced moment-polytope image. If binary witnesses are not complete, determine the least uniform finite alphabet size that is complete.
obligation.obstruction: The proved characterization enumerates \(N!\) common relabellings, \((N!)^K\) arm permutations, all nonempty principal supports in dimension \(K(N-1)\), and their negative eigenspaces. This is finite and exact but not polynomial. A negative cut quadratic form may use several positive adjacent increments in one arm, so the copositivity witness need not be binary. No reduction or structural theorem has been established that either exploits the balanced covariance-moment constraints to remove these enumerations or proves they are unavoidable.
obligation.attempted: Expanded every monotone column in suffix cuts, reduced identity-optimality to explicit copositivity matrices, and reduced noncopositivity to exact strict-positive-eigenspace feasibility over all principal supports. Single-cut inspection was also considered, but mixed cut products in the quadratic form prevent reduction of a general negative witness to one cut per arm.
obligation.partial_result: For every real admissible \(\Omega\), the orbit-membership question is equivalent to the existence of a relabelling \(\pi\) for which finitely many explicit cut matrices \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) are copositive.  Copositivity of each matrix is equivalent to the absence, for every nonempty principal support and every negative real eigenvalue, of a strictly positive vector in the corresponding eigenspace.  With exact real-algebraic inputs this yields a terminating exact root-isolation and ordered-field linear-feasibility algorithm, together with exact multilevel cut witnesses on failure.  The algorithm is exhaustive rather than polynomial, and its witnesses can require up to \(N\) levels per arm.
